lines: [haunted] After that night at the medium... I couldn't leave it alone. I needed to know what was happening to me.
[weary] I went from shop to shop. Amulets, masters... anyone who might know something.
[uneasy] One afternoon, on the top floor of an old mall, I found a shop I had never noticed before.
[uneasy] Nobody else was up there... just an old song, coming from that shop.
[uneasy] Little bottles of oil... with something floating inside. I didn't want to know what.
[uneasy] Old photographs... nobody in them was smiling. And one of them had fresh flowers under it.
[unsettled] Red drinks, with straws in them... for someone who isn't here anymore.
[alarmed, strained] My arm... it's going numb...
[shivering, frightened] So cold... like ice water in my veins...
[frightened whisper] There's someone... standing beside me...
[shaken, sincere] I will not bring you home... but I will make merits under your name.
[reflective] Later, I went to a temple and made a contribution dedicated to her.
[tender, reverent whisper] For the young lady of the amulet... may this merit reach you. May you be at peace.
[reflective] That experience has stayed with me ever since.
[reflective] On another occasion... I was back at the shop I knew best.
[tired, sincere] I'm okay, Uncle. Still trying to understand what happened.
[terrified, straining] No... no... it wants to come in...
[shaken, breathless] I... I have to go.
[breathless, ashamed] I couldn't let anyone see me like that. Not again. Not in public.
[reflective] Eventually, there was one shop owner I visited often. He was the one who noticed.
[awed, calm] Calm... and very old. Like sitting in a forest at night.
[awed, frightened] Something huge... standing right outside.
[awed, uneasy] Water... everywhere. And something moving in it.
[awed, frightened whisper] Everything went quiet. Even them.
[resolute] I wanted to know. So I opened myself... all the way.
[panicking] No... this isn't one of them... this isn't—
[shaken] Twenty minutes... I couldn't remember any of it.
[haunted, reflective] I invited it in, to prove it was there. It came. And I still couldn't tell you what it was.
[haunted] For weeks after, I didn't feel alone. Not once.
[eager] How much, Uncle? I'll try it at home.
[curious, uneasy] Okay... let's see what you are.
[frightened, guilty] I had told her I wouldn't bring her home. And here I was... bringing home something I couldn't even name.
[exhausted, haunted] I didn't sleep that night. Every sound in the room was it... or me.
[reflective] I brought it back the next morning. Some things are not for testing alone.
[polite, tired] Thank you, Uncle... but I think that's enough for today.
[reflective] I put it down and walked away. That much, I got right.
[troubled] But I still didn't understand what I had been doing... or what had been answering me.
[uneasy] And I knew... sooner or later, I would pick something up again.
[sincere] Uncle... I don't want to test them anymore. I don't know what I'm letting in.
[earnest] Do you know anyone who can teach me properly? Someone who really knows?
[resolved, reflective] Discernment. Respect. Proper guidance. That was the first time I asked for them.
[peaceful, certain] You don't need to invite something in... just to prove that something is there.
[haunted] I opened the door to prove it was there. It came in.
[regretful] I brought it home, and broke the promise I made to her.
[uncertain] I put it down. I still didn't understand.
[at peace] I stopped testing, and asked for a teacher.
[an old woman, soft and slow, knowing] You're looking for something special, boy?
[an old woman, soft and slow, a little sad] This one is a Yin amulet. A young lady... she passed away very young. A sad story. But she is very strong.
[an old woman, soft and slow, careful] Hold her gently. If she doesn't like you... put her down.
[an old woman, soft and slow, gentle] She heard your promise.
[an old woman, soft and slow, kind] Go and make merit for her. Don't forget, ah.
[warmly] Ah, you came back! I was worried about you, after Buddha Day.
[excited] Come, come. I just got something new. Hanuman, very powerful one. Come and see.
[alarmed] Eh! Boy! What happened? Your face so pale!
[chanting slowly in a low monotone] Ya-taa waa-ree-wa-haa poo-raa... pa-ree-poo-ren-tee saa-ka-rang... ay-wa-may-wa ee-toh tin-nang... pay-taa-nang oo-pa-kap-pa-tee...
[an old uncle, warm and cheerful] Ah, you're here again. Come, sit, sit. I just made tea.
[an old uncle, warm and curious] You know... I've been watching you. The way you hold the pieces. You have a special sensitivity. Not many people have it.
[an old uncle, warm, encouraging] Here. Hold them, one by one. Let your mind open... and see what you feel.
[an old uncle, pleased and impressed] Ah... you feel it, right? The Lersi. The old hermit.
[an old uncle, impressed] Thao Wessuwan. Guardian of the north. Even he comes for you.
[an old uncle, amazed] Phaya Naga. Wah... all three answer you.
[an old uncle, uncertain, curious] This one... even I don't know what is inside. It came from an old collection. Nobody could tell me. Maybe... you can.
[an old uncle, puzzled, uneasy] Eh... the clock... stopped.
[an old uncle, frightened, shouting] Boy! Boy! Wake up! Can you hear me or not?
[an old uncle, shaken] You fell down. Shaking, talking in a voice... not yours. Twenty minutes, you know!
[an old uncle, sorry, worried] I'm sorry... I shouldn't have given you that one. Here, drink some water. Rest first.
[an old uncle, hesitant, serious] Okay... but treat it with respect, ah. If anything happens, bring it back.
[an old uncle, kind, relieved] Never mind. Better like that. Don't worry about the money.
[an old uncle, approving, gentle] Yes, yes. Don't force. Some things are better left wrapped.
[an old uncle, warm] Come again anytime, ah. Tea is always here.
[an old uncle, thoughtful, humbled] You know... you're right. I only collect them. I don't really know what is inside either.
[an old uncle, warm, sincere] Go and see this temple. There's a monk there who teaches meditation. He will explain it properly. Not like me, play-play.
[an old uncle, gentle] Go. And this one... I'll keep it wrapped.
